params.body:
Nightwatch showed `Exception: Het merk is onbekend` on production (twice in seven days, last today 11:03). That is Nederland Mobiel refusing one vehicle whose make it does not know: HTTP 200 with `<status>error</status>`. The sheet already carries the reason (R P3-5.11) and Beheer > Werking groups it per partner (R P3-15.3); `VehiclePublisher::listOnNederlandMobiel` also sent it through `report()`, so it stood in the alarm layer as an exception on a save that had succeeded. Same lesson as the remove.bg refusals (R S1-6.43) and the RealGarant time-outs (R P3-13.9).

- `App\Exceptions\PartnerRefused`: a typed refusal, still an `Exception` with code 500 and the same message, so every caller that treats a refusal as a failure (the controller, the resend commands, the observer) behaves exactly as before. It carries the partner's name.
- `OwnStockService::sendToNederlandMobiel` throws it for a refused feed and lets it pass through its catch typed; anything else still leaves as the plain exception it was.
- `VehiclePublisher::listOnNederlandMobiel` logs a refusal at info level and reports nothing; no answer or a broken feed is still reported.
- Rule R P3-5.14 amended. Tests: a refusal is on the sheet and not reported, a refusal keeps its type, a partner that does not answer is still reported (`NederlandMobielRefusalIsAFailureTest`).

Not in this PR: the `League\Flysystem\UnableToListContents` from the nightly slide prune is the bucket not answering a listing, already caught and reported by design; three bucket hiccups in three days, worth damping to once an hour if it keeps coming.
params.title: Keep a Nederland Mobiel refusal out of the alarm layer
